latestPosts.caption:
You can have a full diary, a team running around all day with customers coming out of your ears…and still make very little money.

Turnover looks impressive.

Profit pays your bills.

Before you chase another 20 customers, make sure the ones you’ve already got are actually making you money.

Do you know your real profit per cleaning hour?

This bank holiday weekend, I’m doing something I know many cleaning business owners find hard.

I’m switching off.

I’m away at a summer camp for grown-ups with my sister, focusing on fun, fresh air and not thinking about business for a few days.

And honestly? That matters.

Because rest is not a reward you only earn when everything is finished. If you run a business, nothing is ever finished. There is always another message, another rota issue, another client question, another invoice, another job to sort.

So if you can take a proper break this bank holiday, please do. Put the phone down for a while. Go outside. See people you love. Do something that has nothing to do with work.

And if you can’t switch off today, I get it. So many cleaning business owners don’t get bank holidays off. You’re still managing staff, clients, last-minute changes and all the little things that keep the business moving.

But maybe that’s worth paying attention to.

Because your business should not need you every single day, every single weekend, every single bank holiday.

You deserve a business that gives you income, stability and breathing space. Not just a never-ending to-do list.

Happy bank holiday everyone. I hope you get at least a little time that feels like yours and if I can help, send me a message and you'll get a link to auto book into my diary for a one to one (when I'm back of course!)

Friday Focus Tip #46: Know Your Numbers

You can't manage what you don't measure.

Too many cleaning business owners run their business by gut feel. They think they're profitable when they're not. They think they're busy when they could be busier. They have no idea which clients are actually profitable.

Here's what to track:

• Monthly turnover
• Profit margin (target: 25% minimum)
• Cost per clean (wages, products, travel, overheads)
• Number of active clients
• Team size and wages
• Client acquisition cost
• Client retention rate
• Average job value

When you know your numbers, you can make decisions based on facts, not feelings.

You'll spot problems early. You'll know exactly where to focus. You'll understand what's actually working.

The owners building sustainable businesses aren't guessing. They're tracking.

This week, start with one number. Pick the one that matters most to your business right now. Track it. Understand it. Then build from there.

Friday Focus Tip #45: The Power of a Strong Onboarding Process

First impressions matter. A lot.

A strong onboarding process sets the tone for the entire client relationship.

Here's what to include:

• A welcome call or message within 24 hours
• Clear expectations about your service
• Information about your team and standards
• How to contact you with questions
• What to expect on the first clean
• A simple feedback form after the first job
• Follow-up to ask how they felt

When clients feel welcomed and informed, they relax. They trust you. And they're more likely to stick around.

A weak onboarding process? Clients feel uncertain. They compare you to other cleaners. They're more likely to leave.

The best part? A good onboarding process takes minimal time and effort. It just needs to be systematic.
